outcome_intro: This is the MCP server for CIPP, and through CIPP for the Microsoft 365 it manages: Entra ID, Intune, Exchange Online, Defender and GDAP, across every client tenant. It is local-first: one fan-out saves what CIPP returns for each tenant into a SQLite store on your machine, so your AI can search, join and compare that copy offline - per-tenant MFA and Conditional Access tables, the policy one tenant lacks, what changed since your last snapshot - and, from cipp 0.1.13, drive CIPP's writes behind a preview it must confirm.

instead_of_say.instead: Exporting CIPP's MFA report and totalling it per tenant in a spreadsheet before every QBR
instead_of_say.say: Show me MFA registration across every tenant

instead_of_say.instead: Exporting every tenant's Conditional Access policies and comparing them by hand to find the client that is missing one the rest of the fleet has
instead_of_say.say: Which tenants are missing a Conditional Access policy most of my clients have?

instead_of_say.instead: Running the same offboarding steps - block sign-in, convert mailbox, set forwarding - separately in each tenant for a batch of departures, and checking each response by hand to see whether it really worked
instead_of_say.say: Plan the offboarding for this CSV of departures across their tenants

pain_points: CIPP's own views answer questions about the current state. An AI agent working from live answers alone starts over on every question, and comparing this quarter with last needs dated copies you keep yourself.

Scripting CIPP means living with its API limit of 100 requests per 10 seconds per API client (per the CIPP API documentation at docs.cipp.app), and with write endpoints that can answer HTTP 200 while reporting the failure inside the response's Results, so a batch has to read every response to know what happened.

Joining what CIPP returns - which tenant lacks a Conditional Access policy most of the fleet has, what changed in admin roles since last month - is the kind of work an agent can do in seconds from a local copy.

different_vs_wrappers: Most CIPP integrations answer each question with a live call and keep nothing. This connector is local-first: fanout runs a CIPP read once per tenant and, with --save, keeps the rows in a SQLite file on your machine, each save a dated snapshot. The agent can then work across that copy (a per-tenant MFA or Conditional Access table in posture, every stored signal for one tenant in scorecard, the policy one tenant lacks in ca diff) and compare your own snapshots over time (changes, standards drift) without another API call. The cost is one call per tenant and a local copy of tenant data, which you can delete with local-data purge or switch off with CIPP_NO_LOCAL_DATA=1 (both in cipp 0.1.13 and later).
different_vs_vendor: CIPP already answers estate-wide questions itself: its All Tenants views cover the MFA report, Standards alignment and the licence report, its API returns one estate-wide response for tenantFilter=AllTenants, and it ships its own MCP server. If one of those answers your question, use it. This connector complements CIPP rather than replacing it: it keeps a local, dated copy an agent can join and compare offline, and it carries CIPP's full command surface, writes included, behind a preview the agent must confirm (cipp 0.1.13 and later). Microsoft's own Defender tools in its Sentinel MCP server stop at your home tenant: "You can't use this collection as a guest in another tenant or with delegated access" (Microsoft Learn, Sentinel MCP triage tool). This connector reaches every client tenant through the GDAP access CIPP already holds.

faqs.q: Is this an MCP server for Microsoft Defender, Intune, Exchange Online and Entra ID too?
faqs.a: Yes, through your CIPP instance. CIPP manages Microsoft 365 for every client tenant, so this connector reaches what CIPP reaches: Entra ID users, MFA and Conditional Access (`cipp-cli list-mfausers`), Intune policies and Autopilot (`cipp-cli list-intune-policy`), Exchange Online mailboxes, rules and forwarding (`cipp-cli list-mailbox-forwarding`), Defender for Endpoint health, vulnerabilities and incidents (`cipp-cli list-defender-state`, `cipp-cli list-defender-tvm`, `cipp-cli exec-incidents-list`), Defender for Office 365 safe links and anti-phishing, SharePoint and Teams, and GDAP roles and relationships (`cipp-cli list-gdaproles`). If you don't run CIPP, the Microsoft Graph connector talks to Graph directly.

faqs.q: Why not use Microsoft's own Defender MCP server?
faqs.a: Because it only sees your own tenant. Microsoft's Defender tools in the Sentinel MCP server can't be used "as a guest in another tenant or with delegated access" (Microsoft Learn, Sentinel MCP triage tool), so an MSP can't point them at client tenants. This connector reads Defender across every client tenant through the GDAP access your CIPP instance already holds.

Yes, on Plus, Pro, Team, Business, Enterprise, and Education plans (Free tier does not yet expose Developer Mode). ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, not local stdio binaries. The CIPP MCP server runs locally over stdio by default. Its HTTP mode (cipp-mcp --transport http, in cipp 0.1.13 and later) serves http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp, refuses to start until CIPP_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN is set, requires Authorization: Bearer <token> on every request, and needs --tls-cert/--tls-key for any other address. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

The CLI and MCP server run on your machine and talk only to your CIPP instance; MSP Skills receives nothing. But the connector keeps an unencrypted local copy of what it reads (the SQLite store and a five-minute response cache), a learn journal of the commands you ran, and, after auth login, the API client's secret in credentials.toml, so whoever can read your user profile can read them. cipp-cli doctor prints where each file lives, cipp-cli local-data purge --yes (cipp 0.1.13 and later) deletes the store, cache and journal, cipp-cli auth logout removes the stored credentials, and CIPP_NO_LOCAL_DATA=1 (also 0.1.13) keeps no local copy of CIPP data. Removing someone's CIPP access does not touch a copy already on their machine: when a technician leaves, run logout and purge there, delete the checkpoints folder in the CLI's state directory, and rotate the API client's secret in CIPP.

faqs.q: Doesn't CIPP already show this across all tenants?
faqs.a: Often, yes. CIPP's All Tenants views show the MFA report, Standards alignment and the licence report across your estate, and its own MCP server can query AllTenants. This connector does not replace those. It keeps a local, dated copy so an agent can join endpoints and compare your own snapshots offline, and it gives the agent CIPP's write endpoints behind a preview-then-confirm step (cipp 0.1.13 and later).
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: Do I need my own CIPP instance to use this?
faqs.a: Yes - this drives your own self-hosted CIPP instance's API. In CIPP you create an API client (it issues a client ID, secret, tenant ID, and token URL); the CLI authenticates with OAuth2 client credentials via 'cipp-cli auth login', or you pipe a bearer token to 'cipp-cli auth set-token'. It reads and acts through your CIPP - it does not replace it.

faqs.q: Will this hit CIPP's API rate limit?
faqs.a: It can: fanout makes one call per tenant, and CIPP allows 100 requests per 10 seconds per API client. The client waits out HTTP 429 using Retry-After, --concurrency sets how many tenants run at once, and --resume skips tenants a halted run already finished. Once rows are saved, the rollups read the local store and make no API calls.

faqs.q: Can this change my tenants, or only read?
faqs.a: Both. CIPP is a full management API, so the CLI can create users, offboard, set forwarding, and more. In the MCP server (cipp 0.1.13 and later), any CIPP API call that changes something returns a preview first and runs only when the agent confirms it; set CIPP_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 and the server drops its write tools. On the command line, bulk plans by default and writes only with --execute, and other write commands preview with --dry-run. The strongest boundary is still the role you give the API client in CIPP.

faqs.q: Does it replace the CIPP portal?
faqs.a: No. CIPP stays your portal. This connector lets your AI agent work across a local copy of what CIPP returns and drive CIPP from natural language.

governance_summary: The skill drives the cipp-cli and cipp-mcp binaries against your self-hosted CIPP instance, with a bearer token from CIPP_API_KEY or one minted by 'auth login' (kept with the client secret in the CLI's credentials file; with CIPP_NO_CONFIG_WRITE=1, auth login refuses and nothing is stored), sent nowhere except the CIPP API. CIPP is a read-write management API. Read and rollup commands change nothing. In the MCP server (cipp 0.1.13 and later), every CIPP API call that changes something, including every CIPP GET endpoint named as an action, returns a preview and runs only when the agent confirms it, and CIPP_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 drops the write tools. On the command line, bulk prints its plan and only writes with --execute, and other write commands send on run unless you pass --dry-run first. The real permission boundary is the role you grant the API client in CIPP.

safety_tiers.examples: cipp-cli posture --dimension mfa; cipp-cli ca diff; cipp-cli gdap expiring --days 30; cipp-cli fanout --endpoint /ListUsers --all-tenants; cipp-cli list-tenants; cipp-cli doctor
cipp-cli add-user; cipp-cli edit-user; cipp-cli bulk --from changes.csv --execute (plans by default; writes only with --execute)
